20dfbab3b4a6.headline: Google Home update gives Gemini Live a speed boost, a storytelling streak and camera sirens
body: Google has pushed out a fresh round of updates to its Gemini for Home and Google Home apps, according to release notes on its support page, as reported by Digital Trends on November 25. The headline items are a quicker Gemini Live mode, new alarm controls for outdoor cameras and a long list of bug fixes.

Early Access users get the more responsive Gemini Live, which can handle chores like setting a timer or dimming and switching off lights mid-conversation. There is also a new storytelling feature with more dynamic voice and rhythm, and listeners can steer the plot, for instance by granting the hero special abilities. Think bedtime tales with a remote control.

The speed gains are meant to make everyday smart home commands feel less clunky. Gemini should now remember context after you ask it to turn the living room lights back on, and it should stop claiming nothing is playing when you ask it to pause audio. Smart displays can also show a Sources icon indicating where Gemini pulled its information from the web.

In the Home app, the Nest Cam Outdoor (wired, 2nd generation), the onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and the onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired can trigger or silence a 30-second alarm while you watch live footage. The latter two can also use Google Home Premium for Familiar Face notifications. US Premium customers can switch on all premium camera features at once during setup, then decline them one by one. Households with several users can also review video clips together in selected areas.

Nest thermostat owners can copy one day's schedule onto other days. The rest is housekeeping: camera notification previews return on Android 17, video playback issues are reduced, landscape controls no longer clash with the Pixel's camera hole, and the iOS color picker is simpler. Google Home Speaker, stereo, Google TV and music-sharing features should also be more reliable.
Most changes arrive through the Home app, but Gemini Live will take a couple of weeks to reach all Early Access households.
20dfbab3b4a6.summary: Google's November 25 Home update makes Gemini Live faster, adds steerable stories, lets some outdoor cameras sound a 30-second alarm, and simplifies Premium camera setup in the US, plus many fixes.
20dfbab3b4a6.pixel_take: Your smart home can now tell a bedtime story where the hero gets superpowers, and also sound a siren at your porch. Range, honestly.
20dfbab3b4a6.why_it_matters: Smart home platforms are competing on how useful AI assistants feel day to day, and speed and memory are what decide that. Bundling Premium camera features at setup also nudges more users toward a subscription, which affects what households spend on home security.
key_points: Gemini Live in Early Access is faster, remembers context and adds steerable storytelling.
Three outdoor cameras get a 30-second alarm; two gain Familiar Face alerts with Premium.
Gemini Live will take a couple of weeks to reach all Early Access households.

0cd196b5fc14.headline: Netflix's coziest show returned after seven years, and almost nobody noticed
body: A new season of Midnight Diner: Tokyo Stories is streaming on Netflix, but according to The Verge, it has returned with almost no fanfare. The season's first episode premiered in October, and the writer says they found it only by accident.

The show centers on a small restaurant in the backstreets of Shinjuku that opens only from midnight to 7:00AM. Its late-night regulars help one another under the eye of the owner, known simply as "master" and played by Kaoru Kobayashi. The series aired for three seasons on Japanese TV before Netflix picked it up for more under the Tokyo Stories subtitle.

The gap is the notable part. Season 2 of the Netflix run streamed in 2019, so fans waited seven years. The wait was long enough that the new season opens with an episode about the diner's struggles during the pandemic, complete with regulars peeking outside to see whether it had reopened.

After that, it is back to form. Each episode is built around a dish, from spicy konjac to pork cutlet sandwiches, and uses it to tell a story. The Verge praises the mix of warmth and heartbreak, saying it is as likely to make you laugh as cry.
Netflix is also doing something unusual: it is not releasing the whole season at once. New episodes arrive every Tuesday, and six of a planned 10 are out so far.

The Verge's complaint is about visibility. The only promotion it could find was a trailer on Netflix's Japanese YouTube channel, and even a devoted rewatcher got no notification. As the service fills up with reality shows, live programming and games, the argument goes, its hidden gems get harder to spot.
0cd196b5fc14.summary: Midnight Diner: Tokyo Stories is back on Netflix after seven years with almost no promotion, according to The Verge. Six of 10 new episodes are out, with weekly releases every Tuesday.
0cd196b5fc14.pixel_take: Netflix spent seven years away from its most comforting show and then forgot to mention it was back. Even a midnight diner gets better foot traffic than that.
0cd196b5fc14.why_it_matters: As streaming catalogs balloon, discovery becomes a real problem for both viewers and the platforms that want them to stay subscribed. Shows that go unnoticed can be wasted content spend, and weekly releases show Netflix experimenting beyond binge drops.
key_points: A new season of Midnight Diner: Tokyo Stories is streaming, seven years after season 2 in 2019.
Six of a planned 10 episodes are out, with new ones every Tuesday.
The Verge says promotion was minimal, with only a trailer on Netflix's Japanese YouTube channel.

ea925af610dc.headline: Ufologist Spots Alien 'Doorway' on Mars; Fellow UFO Researcher Says It's Just Rocks
body: UFO researcher Scott C Waring claims photos from NASA's Perseverance rover show proof of an ancient Martian civilisation, according to Metro. Writing on his blog UFO Sightings Daily last week, he pointed to a panorama taken in November 2022.

Waring says the image shows a seven-foot-tall doorway leading into an 'adobe-like house', plus a fallen green-blue statue of what he called an alien god. He argues the statue's colour appears nowhere else in the photo.
NASA says the images were captured around 1.30pm solar time at Cape Nukshak, near Jezero Crater. That 30-mile-wide pit once held an ancient river, back when Mars was warmer and wetter.

Scientists think that era may have had the ingredients for life, but the likely residents were single-cell microbes, not statue-building neighbours. That is why Perseverance hunts for tiny traces in rocks rather than anything resembling Martian dinosaurs.

Even a fellow UFO researcher isn't buying it. Filmmaker Mark Christopher Lee told Metro the claim is classic pareidolia, the brain finding familiar shapes in random rocks, and said NASA's original image shows geological features, not architecture.

NASA has not declared proof of life on Mars. Last year it said Perseverance found a lump of hardened mud that was the 'clearest sign of life' so far, with minerals that may be biosignatures from 3.5 billion years ago. Lee added that ideas such as life seeding Earth via Martian meteorites are legitimate lines of inquiry, but a doorway in one low-resolution frame is not evidence.
ea925af610dc.summary: A UFO researcher says a NASA Mars rover photo shows an alien doorway and statue. A fellow UFO researcher told Metro it's pareidolia, and NASA has not confirmed life on Mars.
ea925af610dc.pixel_take: Mars has had billions of years to build a front door, and the best candidate is a rock. Even fellow ufologists are saying the landlord should check the listing again.
ea925af610dc.why_it_matters: Viral space claims show how easily low-resolution images spread, and why careful verification matters. Real Mars science, like the search for biosignatures, drives funding and technology in the growing space sector.
key_points: Scott C Waring claims a 2022 Perseverance panorama shows a doorway and statue.
Fellow UFO researcher Mark Christopher Lee calls it pareidolia, saying NASA's image shows geology.
NASA has not declared proof of life on Mars, though one rock sample is its clearest sign so far.

abfa18c13c7e.headline: EPA Chief Zeldin Says Air Monitors Found No Airborne Lead After Army's Iowa Detonation
body: The Environmental Protection Agency said Thursday that its air monitors have detected no airborne lead following the Army's controlled detonation of thousands of pounds of unstable explosives in southeastern Iowa, according to The Hill. The headline attributes the finding to EPA chief Lee Zeldin.

The detonation took place a day before the agency's update. The Hill's teaser indicates the EPA is still continuing its work in the area, though the material available does not say what that work involves or how long it will last.

Controlled detonations are a standard way to dispose of explosives considered too unstable to move or store safely. The tradeoff is that burning or blowing up such material can raise questions about what ends up in the air, soil and water nearby, which is why environmental monitoring typically follows.

Lead is the specific worry here because it is a heavy metal that can be harmful to people when inhaled or ingested, and it can be released by certain munitions-related materials. A reading of no detected airborne lead is reassuring, but it covers only what monitors picked up in the air, not necessarily other contaminants or other exposure routes.

The full details, including where the monitors were placed, how many there are and what the EPA plans next, were not available in the material we reviewed. We will update this story if more specifics emerge.
abfa18c13c7e.summary: The EPA says its air monitors found no airborne lead after the Army's controlled detonation of thousands of pounds of unstable explosives in southeastern Iowa, though the agency's work there continues.
abfa18c13c7e.why_it_matters: Environmental checks after military disposal operations affect local health, property values and public trust in federal agencies. Clean air readings can ease community fears and limit cleanup costs, but continued monitoring shows regulators are not ready to declare the matter closed.
key_points: EPA says its monitors detected no airborne lead after the Army's detonation in southeastern Iowa.
The Army destroyed thousands of pounds of unstable explosives in a controlled blast.
The EPA's work in the area is still ongoing, according to The Hill.

cb4c4139de5a.headline: Two Italian technicians killed in Kuwait drone strike; Iran denies it was behind the attack
body: Two Italian nationals working as technicians for German arms maker Rheinmetall were killed in a strike on a facility in Kuwait, Italy's foreign ministry said, according to BBC News. Italian and Kuwaiti authorities have blamed Iran, which denies any responsibility.

Kuwait's defence ministry had earlier said four people were injured by falling shrapnel after several drones from Iran were detected and intercepted. Those hurt were the two Italians, a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani national. Kuwait's army described the target as a "vital site" and called the incident "heinous Iranian aggression".

Italian press agency Ansa, citing the foreign ministry, reported that the two men were at an air defence detection station doing maintenance on systems used by Kuwait's armed forces. Italian media named them and said one was 36 and the other 65 and nearing retirement. Italy's foreign minister was quoted as saying investigations showed the drone was made in Iran, and that Iranian proxies are known to carry out attacks in the region.

Tehran rejected the accusation. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the incident "suspicious", said Iran would work with Kuwait and Italy to determine the cause, and described it as a "precooked recipe for war". He said he had offered condolences to his Italian and Kuwaiti counterparts. An armed forces spokesperson said Iran had conducted no military or offensive operations.

The strike comes just over a week after Kuwait said it repelled Iranian drone attacks on an airbase hosting US forces, the first on the country in more than two months. The wider war began in late February when the US and Israel attacked Iran, which retaliated against Israel and Gulf states hosting US assets. Recent exchanges of fire and stalled talks have raised fears of escalation.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni offered condolences to the families. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called for more pressure on Iran, saying Gulf security is a security issue for Europe too.
cb4c4139de5a.summary: Two Italian Rheinmetall technicians died in a strike on a Kuwaiti facility that Kuwait and Italy blame on Iran. Tehran denies involvement and calls the incident suspicious, as fears of wider escalation grow.
cb4c4139de5a.why_it_matters: The deaths of European civilians working for a defence contractor pull Europe closer to a Gulf conflict that has so far mostly involved the US and Israel. Escalation in the region tends to rattle oil prices, shipping and markets, and can affect defence stocks and inflation.
key_points: Two Italian Rheinmetall technicians were killed in a strike on a facility in Kuwait.
Kuwait and Italy blame Iran; Tehran denies responsibility and calls the incident suspicious.
The attack follows recent Iranian drone strikes on Kuwait and stalled US-Iran negotiations.
